draft.title: The Australian Consumer Law
card: The Australian Consumer Law (ACL) is a national law that applies across Australia. It sets rules that sellers must follow when dealing with consumers.
Consumer guarantees
automatic rights that come with goods and services. For example, goods must be of acceptable quality, and services must be provided with due care and skill.
Misleading conduct
the ACL bans misleading or deceptive conduct. A seller breaks this rule if its words, ads or actions give buyers a false impression.
Unfair terms

the ACL bans unfair contract terms in standard form contracts offered to consumers. A term can be unfair if it creates a big imbalance in the parties' rights and is not needed to protect the seller's legitimate interests.
draft.remember: The ACL guarantees basic standards and bans false impressions and unfair terms.

a.q: Ravi buys a new kettle in Newcastle. It stops working after two days of normal use. Which part of the ACL does this most directly involve?
opts: A consumer guarantee of acceptable quality
The ban on unfair contract terms
The ban on misleading advertising
A guarantee of due care and skill
a.why: Goods must be of acceptable quality, and a new kettle that fails after two days of normal use is unlikely to meet that standard. Due care and skill applies to services, not to goods such as a kettle.
a.clue: A kettle is goods, not a service.

b.q: A gym in Parramatta advertises 'no joining fees' but charges a joining fee when members sign up. Which ACL rule is the gym most likely to have breached?
opts: The ban on misleading or deceptive conduct
The ban on unfair contract terms
The guarantee of acceptable quality
The guarantee of due care and skill
b.why: The advertisement gave customers a false impression about the cost, which is misleading or deceptive conduct. It is not mainly about an unfair term, because the problem is the false claim in the ad rather than an imbalance of rights in a contract.
b.clue: Focus on what the advertisement told people.

a.best: A consumer guarantee of acceptable quality

b.best: The ban on misleading or deceptive conduct

problems.detail: The right option, 'A consumer guarantee of acceptable quality', is clearly the longest. It is also the only one with the extra word 'consumer', so it stands out from the other options.

problems.detail: The unfair terms test is incomplete. Under the ACL, a term is unfair only if it meets all three parts of the test. It must cause a significant imbalance, not be reasonably necessary to protect the seller's legitimate interests, and cause detriment to the consumer if relied on. The card leaves out detriment, so a student could think two parts are enough. The word 'can' softens this but does not fix it.
